proposed_assumptions.condition: Fix the following computational conventions, used for every complexity claim in this paper: (i) for a finite simple bow-free ADMG \(G\) on vertex set \(U\) with \(|U|=n\), singleton target \(s\), and positive rational cost \(c\), the supplied total order on \(U\) induces the order isomorphism \(U\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,n\), and the instance is encoded as the resulting \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-carrier tuple of directed and bidirected adjacency bit-matrices, the index of \(s\), and the numerators and denominators of \(c\) in binary, of encoding length \(L=\operatorname{poly}(n,\operatorname{bitlen}(c))\), while every statement of the form ``\(X\) is computable in polynomial time'' means that the induced map on canonically encoded \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) instances is computable in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(L\); (ii) all predicates and objective values appearing in this paper, namely \(\mathcal C(G,s)\), \(r(G,s)\), \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\), \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\), and feasibility of an intervention set, are invariant under vertex relabeling, so a polynomial-time algorithm on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) carrier transfers to any finite vertex type \(U\) via the supplied order with polynomial overhead; (iii) an algorithm performing \(\operatorname{poly}(n,L)\) elementary operations on encoded instances, consisting of graph adjacency queries, reachability and ancestor searches, comparisons, and field operations on rationals of bit length \(\operatorname{poly}(L)\), runs in time \(\operatorname{poly}(n,L)\); and (iv) the class of polynomial-time maps on canonically encoded instances is closed under composition, in particular under composition of the private-guard expansion, parent-spouse rounding, and reverse guard-replacement map.
proposed_assumptions.reason: The active repair directive requires this already user-approved convention so that every runtime and hardness claim is typed on one canonical encoded carrier and transferred back only by the declared relabeling rule; its four approved clauses are preserved and joined into one LaTeX-valid assumption sentence to satisfy atomic-assumption hygiene.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This convention constrains only encoding, bit complexity, relabeling, and closure of polynomial-time maps. It supplies no hedge, rank, feasibility, objective, approximation-ratio, or hardness conclusion.

proposed.statement: Assign unit cost to every vertex of \(G_H\). Every vertex cover \(C\subseteq U\) maps to the intervention \(\{x_u:u\in C\}\) with the same cost, and every feasible intervention maps in polynomial time, by replacing each selected \(z_e\) with an endpoint of \(e\), to a vertex cover of no larger cost. Therefore \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\). The reduction is an \(L\)-reduction with constants one, so rank-three MCID is \(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard even with unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree; the \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness remains for source graphs of maximum degree three.
proposed.justification: Objective preservation identifies the exact complexity transition at the first nonempty rank rather than importing generic three-hitting-set hardness.
proposed.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove unrestricted MCID hardness, while Alimonti and Kann supply cubic vertex-cover hardness; neither gives a promise-preserving rank-three causal realization.
proposed.consumer: The result supplies canonically encoded structured hard instances on which the RC2 and Gurobi formulations can be evaluated without uncontrolled hedge rank.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The approved uniform computational-model assumption is now a direct dependency of the polynomial guard-replacement map and the hardness reduction; the formal claim itself is unchanged.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), every nonempty \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) has size three and meets both \(P_s\) and \(T_s\). For an optimal \(y\) of the natural covering relaxation, every \(A_t\) is feasible for \(0<t<1/2\), and some breakpoint choice satisfies \(\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). Such a choice is found in polynomial time by the promised-rank enumerator using the supplied order.
proposed.justification: The parent-spouse crossing property improves the generic factor three for rank-three hitting set to the vertex-cover threshold two.
proposed.gap: Elahi and coauthors explicitly leave efficient MCID approximation as future work, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give only logarithmic approximation in general and exact polynomial algorithms through residual size two.
proposed.consumer: On the canonical encoding, and hence on a supplied finite carrier by relabeling, the theorem provides a deterministic warm start with an auditable factor-two guarantee for the existing ILP and WPMAX-SAT workflows.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\) and a fixed promised rank bound \(r_0\), all inclusion-minimal residual hedges can be output exactly once, in the lexicographic order induced by the supplied order, in time \(|V|^{r_0+O(1)}\) and polynomial space. At \(r_0=3\) in the present bow-free singleton model, the runtime is \(O(|V|^3\operatorname{poly}(|V|))\). Given \(k\), branching on an uncovered residual returns the least-cost feasible intervention among sets of cardinality at most \(k\), or certifies that none exists, in \(O(3^k\operatorname{poly}(|V|,L))\), where \(L\) is the cost-encoding length.
proposed.justification: The proposition uses the supplied causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\), together with the rank promise, to provide the exact-once lexicographic obstruction list assumed by the LP, while scoping exact weighted search to a supplied cardinality bound.
proposed.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash note polynomial subset enumeration at fixed hedge size, while Fernau assumes an explicit hyperedge list; neither supplies exact-once causal output together with the bounded-cardinality scope correction.
proposed.consumer: The canonical causal-vertex-ordered enumerator, transferred by relabeling to generic finite carriers, is a deterministic rank-informed front end for Akbari and coauthors' software and for Elahi and coauthors' exact solver encodings.

proposed.statement: Given a supplied total order on \(V\), enumerate all minimal residual hedges of size at most three in the induced lexicographic order, optimize or two-approximate that relaxation, and verify the returned \(A\) by alternating restriction of \(G[V\setminus A]\) to directed ancestors of \(s\) and the bidirected component of \(s\). If verification succeeds, an exact relaxation optimum is globally exact and the rounded answer costs at most \(2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\). If verification fails, deletion-based minimization returns a verifiable \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) with \(|R|>3\).
proposed.justification: The interface safely exploits low rank without pretending to recognize the promise from a successful run.
proposed.gap: The WPMAX-SAT and ILP formulations of Elahi and coauthors solve unrestricted MCID but do not return a violated-rank certificate, while explicit bounded-rank hitting-set algorithms assume the promise externally.
proposed.consumer: On the canonical encoding, with relabeling transfer to a supplied finite carrier, RC2 and Gurobi users receive either a certified solution guarantee or a concrete large hedge for the unrestricted backend.

proposed.statement: For every \(F\subseteq V\) with \(s\in F\), alternating restriction to the vertices that reach \(s\) in \(D\) and to the bidirected component of \(s\) terminates in polynomial time at a fixed set \(F^{\star}\). prose_updates.tldr: Under the standard positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics, acquiring \(Q[V\setminus A]=P(V\setminus A\mid\operatorname{do}(A))\) identifies the causal target \(Q_s\) exactly when \(A\) hits every minimal residual hedge. Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMGs, and four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes every finite graph edge clutter and yields unit-cost \(\mathsf{NP}\)- and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under \(r(G,s)\leq3\), exact promised enumeration and parent-spouse thresholding give a weighted factor-two algorithm; complete-graph expansions show that the natural-LP gap supremum is two, and the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \((2-\epsilon)\) lower bound transfers to the unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. Every polynomial-time assertion is made on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded carrier, with polynomial rational bit complexity and guarded composition, and then transferred to a generic finite supplied-ordered carrier by relabeling invariance. The optimizer-or-rank-violation interface does not claim unrestricted rank recognition or unconstrained weighted \(3^k\) optimization.

project_justification.fill: The paper imports the positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian hedge-hitting identification bridge, then proves the four-vertex obstruction classification, exact private-guard realization, objective-preserving hardness, and the exact weighted natural-LP gap two at promised rank three. Source expansions use an order \(\prec\) on \(U\), while promised enumeration uses a distinct causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\). All algorithmic and reduction maps are stated first on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded carrier with binary rational costs; elementary graph and rational operations and guarded compositions have polynomial cost there, and relabeling invariance transfers the outputs and objective guarantees to arbitrary finite supplied-ordered carriers. Complete-graph gadgets provide the matching gap sequence, the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \((2-\epsilon)\) threshold holds on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass, and the bounded-cardinality and optimizer-or-violation interfaces retain their promised scope.
project_justification.gap: The published minimum-cost intervention-design frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness, but it does not identify the first nonempty finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank, the exact weighted natural-LP gap at that boundary, or the approximation threshold on a graphically sparse hard subclass.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every minimal residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition. This structure controls every positive-rational-cost instance under the rank promise, while private guards still realize every graph edge clutter inside the narrower unit-cost class whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree.

prose_updates.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes supply the finite simple ADMG and bow-free conventions. Shpitser and Pearl provide the complete hedge obstruction, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash give its positive-compatible proxy-intervention formulation and the minimum-weight hedge-hitting program. They prove unrestricted hardness and polynomial solvability through residual size two; this paper establishes the first nonempty bow-free singleton boundary and its rank-three approximation frontier. Elahi and coauthors' RC2 and Gurobi formulations are direct computational consumers. Alimonti and Kann supply cubic Vertex Cover \(\mathsf{APX}\)-completeness, Khot and Regev supply the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional factor-two graph threshold, and Korte and Vygen supply rational linear-programming in polynomial input time. Those imported complexity statements are used on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded carrier fixed here; relabeling invariance, polynomial rational bit complexity, and closure under guarded composition transfer the resulting algorithms and reductions to generic finite supplied-ordered carriers. Singh's source LP-gap formula is only motivation for the independently proved complete-graph calculation, and Fernau's branching result informs only the scoped cardinality-bounded search. No unrestricted rank-three recognizer is claimed.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The factor-two algorithm is promise-based: polynomial enumeration is guaranteed only after \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and a causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\) are supplied, and a successful optimizer run does not certify the rank bound. The order \(\triangleleft_V\) controls only lexicographic output and differs from the source order \(\prec\). The \(O(3^k)\) exact-search guarantee requires a supplied cardinality bound \(k\). Polynomial time means polynomial in \(n\) and the canonical binary encoding length \(L\) on the \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) carrier; transfer to a generic finite type requires its supplied order and the declared relabeling invariance. Finite-sample allocation and statistical estimation remain outside this combinatorial identification-design result.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal bridge is imported under positive-compatible recursive semi-Markovian semantics; no finite-sample or weaker-positivity extension is claimed. The exact weighted gap supremum covers positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and nonempty clutter, whereas the matching hardness subclass has unit costs and a radius-two bidirected tree. Every polynomial-time map is interpreted on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-encoded adjacency-and-cost representation and transferred to a generic finite supplied-ordered carrier only through relabeling invariance; rational field operations are charged at binary bit complexity and guarded compositions remain polynomial. The source order \(\prec\) and causal enumeration order \(\triangleleft_V\) are distinct. Rank-at-most-three recognition, planar realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open, and weighted \(O(3^k)\) search is asserted only with a supplied cardinality bound.
